what_this_is: What is waiting on the person: everything only they can do (sign in, approve, answer, pay, press a button somewhere) gathered from every place it is kept into one answer, read by the shared card-sections reader (src/card-sections.mjs) in the person's own store (src/person-store.mjs waitingOnYou). tool:what-is-waiting-on-me answers it, the workflow for purpose "tell-the-person-what-waits" has every AI show it in the chat at its start and after its work (named in src/server-instructions.json), and Home's Waiting for you card shows the same rows. `list` is the person's own Waiting on you list, made the first time it is read: any AI that cannot do something itself keeps it there as a row (put_list_rows, one row per thing, with a short id naming it so adding it again changes the same row), and a row marked Done leaves the answer and stays done: its status settles on Done (src/lists.mjs), so an AI putting the same ask again cannot reopen it (null clears it on purpose), and a list made before a field property was added gains it on the next read. `sources` say where each kind of ask is read and how its card reads (`card` maps each card field to paths, the first holding a value wins, or a fixed { value }), `opens` is the screen it opens in Trillion (or the item's own `link`), and `address` is the page it opens on the web, filled from the item's fields. `sections` are the rows in order, most urgent first: each `read` names a source, `where` keeps only items passing every test (equals, not, one_of, none_of, at_least, at_most, present), `newest` sorts by a path, `distinct` keeps one card per value of a path; `limit` caps it; `action` is the words of what the person does; `on_home: false` leaves a row off Home when Home already asks it another way; `points_at` is the control a walkthrough points at when the person is taken to one of the row's things (tool:take-me-there, src/take-me-there.mjs), a selector with {item} standing for the thing's own id. `said` sums it up in one sentence for a chat or a notice. A new kind of ask is one source and one section here. Each section's `step` says what its things are as one step for src/who-does-it.mjs (`needs`, `only_a_person_because` a reason id of its `only_a_person` rows, `given_in.saved_instruction` the id of the saved instruction that records consent the person gave once): every card is weighed on it at the one reader before any section is cut to its `limit` (src/waiting-weigh.mjs; a card an AI filed with its own `needs` or `reason_id` is weighed on those), and only what says `you` or `one-tap` is shown. The AIs are the default doer: the rest is handed to them once each (a section's `step.job` and `step.said` say what its things are to them, else `nudge.weigh`; a section whose `step.already_ais` is true lists things that already are hand-offs to the AIs, such as stuck work, so they leave the person's view and no second job is made for them), in the one `order` below, so nothing leaves the person's view without an AI holding it; the same title twice in a section shows once. `order` is the one order of everything shown across sections (answer.order): what holds up most first (`blocks`), then the newest. 2026-10-11: drafts the person had already approved, files from AI tests, stuck AI jobs and decisions their AIs opened from their own words were shown to them as theirs. `assigned` is every thing in the person's spaces given to them (its `assignee` fact names them, by the name they show there or their member id; src/spaces.mjs assignedTo), so a thing someone gives a member in a space reaches that member here, with every nudge and device, not only when they open the space; `done_facts` are the facts Done sets on the thing in its space, so every member sees it done. `done_when_connected` is the path to a fact naming a service: a given thing carrying it (such as the connect step Trillion gives a member whose calendar is not connected, src/space-calendars.json `ask`) is done by itself once the person has that service connected, by whatever road they connected it, its `done_facts` set in its space so it leaves. Home draws the sections in their order above its board as the person's Needs you stack (src/workspace/needs-you.tsx), forcefully and on every board, under the person's show rules (subject needs-you): each row is one section with how many wait, its newest card, the section's `action` as one press, a `clip` to play when a card carries one, and a `form` when the action needs an answer (`runs`: Workshop tools run in order, each input value taken from the card (`card`), a form box (`field`) or fixed (`value`); a run with `when` needs every named box or card field filled). `finish` names the `finishes` row a section's cards are finished by when a card names none (src/workspace/waiting-queue.ts finishOf); `all_done` is the words of a press that marks every card of a source that is done by being opened (`done_by_opening`) as done; done marks are kept in the person's fact `done.fact`, the newest `done.most`. A source's `opens.screen` and `opens.input` may be paths, read from each item. A row of the person's own list whose `checked_by` rule (src/lists.json kind checked-by) passes on one device's facts (src/device-facts.mjs, reported by the person's own pages and apps) is set Done by itself when what waits is read and whenever a device reports, so a step a device can see for itself (a camera plugged in, a switch turned on) ticks itself. A row's `done_when_rule` (src/lists.json kind done-when-rule, src/done-when.mjs, src/done-when-facts.json) is a check Trillion makes itself against what is true now (saved logins, connections, device facts, files, work, another list): every read of what waits checks every waiting row's rule, a row whose rule passes is set Done with `closed_because` "Checked: <says>", and the same check runs shortly after any source changes (src/live-screen.mjs revisions, the saved logins, list rows and device facts writes), so it closes with no screen open. Every asks card carries `check` { state: done | not_yet | cannot_check | failed, words, checked_at } so a screen never has to say "Checking..." for more than a moment: not_yet says the real counts ("740 of 741 logins your AIs can read"), a row with no rule says Trillion cannot check it, and a check that threw or took over 5 seconds says it will try again. A notice about a row (src/waiting-ask-notices.mjs, src/waiting-nudge.mjs, any tell whose refs.card is `asks:<row id>`) is checked again right before it is sent (tell-the-person beforeSend, person-store waitingNoticeGuard) and not sent when the row is Done or its rule now passes. `nudge`: while anything has waited `after_minutes`, the person is told, louder the longer it waits (src/waiting-nudge.mjs, on the store's scheduler; the owner 2026-10-06: "Hey, we are waiting on you", escalating until it's done). Each `ladder` rung is reached when the oldest thing has waited its `after_minutes` and tells with its notice `kind` at most every `every_minutes` and `most_per_day` times a day; a rung with `board` keeps everything waiting on every live board (the iPhone's Live Activity and lock screen, the Mac menu bar, widgets) as the one running notice `board` (its words filled with {count}, {first}: the oldest thing's title, and {section}: the title of the row it is in, so it never shows a bare name such as one service's), ended quietly with `ended_kind` once nothing waits; a rung with `take_over` also opens the oldest thing itself on the open Trillion page (tool:take-me-there). Every notice opens the oldest thing's own address, `open` only when it has none inside Trillion. Before it asks, it weighs (src/who-does-it.mjs): a row an AI put on the list with what it `needs` and no `only_you_because` that Trillion can do is handed to the AIs with `weigh.job` and never shown to the person; a row that names a known reason (`reason_id`, such as a sign-in only they can give) is weighed on it with the helper that already tried (`tried_doer`), so a sign-in goes to the AIs holding the saved logins first and reaches the person only after one was stopped, so only what truly needs them is in their face. Voices are the speakers no one has named yet: labels matching `pattern` among the newest messages (messages.unnamedSpeakers), each with the newest clip a turn of it carried (computer/listen.mjs attaches one per voice), and `voice` when its label part matches `voice_pattern`; a voice whose turns carried no clip gets the moment it was heard in the sound the listener kept, found by its last words (`clip`: the newest `searches` voices per read, asked only of the search mechanisms `matches` names (the words in transcripts: a voice's own words are found by its words, and asking the meaning lanes read every kept vector, 1.5 million rows a read of this answer on the person's store on 2026-10-06), answers kept in the fact `fact`, a miss asked again after `retry_minutes`), drawn as `clip_at` seconds into that recording. A row of the person's own list may carry the `device` it is about (the model, such as ILCE-7M4; src/device-rows.mjs): it is shown only to someone whose devices or files show that device, and `devices` says how that is told. A row about a device nothing of theirs shows is left out of every reader (what waits, the hold, the reminders and the board, take-me-there, the lists reads) because all of them read through the person store's waitingOnYou, and a notice about it is not sent (waitingNoticeGuard). An AI filing a step that only an owner of one kind of device can do (a camera, a printer) puts that device's model in `device`, so everyone else is never asked.

sessions._what: Where in time each app heard speakers nobody has named (src/voice-sessions.mjs): one row per stretch of listening, each covering its app from its first_at to the next stretch and listing every unnamed label heard in it. A store with turns kept before the rows builds them build_pages pages of build_page messages per scheduler step; until then the voices read says `preparing` instead of answering from part of them.

guess._what: Who a heard voice probably is, from evidence the account already holds (src/voice-guesses.mjs). Each source that matches a person's row adds its weight and its `why` words ({name} the guessed name, {text} the words that matched); a row is matched by its whole title, or by its first word when that word has at least first_word_letters letters (then for first_word_share of the weight), on whole words, ignoring case and accents. The people are the rows of every list that holds people (lists.json holds), at most people_most. `said` is a name someone else said in the voice's conversation, within `said.minutes` of the voice's first and last turn and from at most `said.reads` messages; each source's `scope` says what its evidence is about: `voice` (this voice itself: the listener's own guess, a name chosen before for the same guess) or `moment` (the recording or the time it was heard in: its title, its file's own name without folders, the calendar, a name said nearby), the same for every voice heard there. Only voice evidence folds voices into one row or keeps a voice in another script from being left out as playback; a moment guess is preselected (`sure`) only when no other listed voice of that moment carries it.

before_asking._what: A row that asks the person for FACTS (a past-event ask such as what happened, how it went, how many were bought: `asks`, read in `ask_fields`; a plain request like 'describe the logo you want' or 'how many seats should we book' is never caught) must first have the person's connected arrivals read (src/waiting-filing.mjs rowArrivalsRefusal, a done-when check over `arrived`, src/done-when-facts.json). The window is the row's about_from..about_until (else the last `default_hours` hours) and the places are `routes` (each a live carrier route that captures what happened in the world: Photos, Voice Memos, Listening, watch, Screenshots; never an AI-chat carrier such as Claude Code or Codex, which arrive constantly). When something arrived there, the filing is refused listing the arrivals, so the AI reads them (a server cannot interpret footage or audio) and files again with `read_field` saying which it read and what they showed, naming at least one of them, and asking only for what they leave out; or does not ask at all. Why it exists: 2026-10-11 a card asked 'Say what happened at the Target shelf today' for a 4-6pm shelf test and said nothing reached Trillion, while 98 Photos items from that window had arrived (route Photos, /Photos/2026-10) and voice memos with transcripts had arrived on 2026-10-06. It asked him to repeat what his sources already brought. A check that cannot be made (a source too slow) never blocks a filing.
before_asking.asks: \b(say what happened|what happened (at|in|during)|tell (me|us|trillion) what (happened|you saw|they did)|how did\b.*\bgo\b|how many\b.*\b(did|were|picked|bought|stopped|came)\b|walk (me|us) through what happened|report what happened|give (me|us) the (counts|results) (from|of))\b

words.refused: "{title}" was not filed: it asks the person for facts, but {count} of their own arrivals from {from} to {until} already cover it ({places}). Read them first, then file it again. Newest first: {arrivals}{more}. Look at the Photos items and read the voice memos' transcripts, then put in {read_field} which you read and what they showed (name at least one by its file name), and ask only for what they leave out; if they answer it, do not ask at all. If the window is wrong, set {from_field} and {until_field} to the time it is really about.

unchecked._what: A step filed with its done described in words (`words_field`) but no rule Trillion checks (the list's field of kind `rule_kind`, src/done-when.mjs) waits until the person says it is done, and every AI keeps putting it in front of them meanwhile. put_list_rows keeps the row and names it under `unchecked` in its answer, with what Trillion can check, so the AI that filed it adds the rule while it can (src/waiting-filing.mjs uncheckedWaitingRows). Why it exists: on 2026-10-09 a certificate step said it was done when 'A Developer ID Application certificate file is in your Downloads folder'; the certificate arrived at 17:58, the Mac reported the download, and with no rule nothing looked, so the hold kept putting the step in the person's face.
unchecked.said: "{title}" says it is done when "{done_when}", but nothing checks that, so it waits until the person says so. If one of these can see it, put done_when_rule on the row so it closes by itself: {sources}.

rounds._what: Work that runs in rounds (src/work-rounds.mjs): a row whose step_field holds words finishes only this round. Done counts the round in done_field, appends log_line (what the round showed) to log_field, opens next_field (else the same step) as the new step and restarts starts_field, so it waits again with its progress; once planned_field is reached the row is done the ordinary way.

hold.what_this_is: The hold (trillion-workshop tools/hold-one-thing-until-done/read-data/needs-you-hold.mjs, drawn over every Trillion page by src/workspace/needs-you-hold.tsx): while it is on, any page the person opens shows the ONE thing that needs them most, nothing else reachable, until it is done or set aside with a reason. the owner 2026-10-06: 'only one thing you can do, so the river flows in that one direction'. `held_fact`: the one thing held now, kept from every Waiting on you read and handed to every AI's turn (POST /notices/unseen `held`, harness/decisions-since.mjs). `devices`: the tools run on the person's own devices when the held thing changes (`when_held`: the Mac keeps only Trillion open, the Workshop tool tools/hold-a-computer-quiet, run by computer/mac-tools.mjs; tool:take-me-there opens the held thing on every open Trillion page and tells the person on every channel its notice kind reaches, with the link that opens it on any device, so the held thing reaches them by Trillion itself, an AI chat included, and no AI has to paste it) and when nothing is held any more (`when_free`); `{key}` and `{title}` in a run's input are the held thing's (trillion-workshop tools/hold-one-thing-until-done/read-data/needs-you-hold.mjs heldInput); a new device lock or a new way to reach the person is a row here. `after_minutes`: how long a thing waits before it holds the page. `aside`: setting the thing aside needs `min_words` of reason, lasts `minutes`, `most_per_day` times a day, and each reason goes to the AIs as `job`. `hand_back`: when the person's part is done, or the thing does not work where they are, one of its `ways` hands the rest to the AIs with their words (`min_words`) as that way's `job`; the thing leaves the hold for `keep_days` while the AIs check, finish, fix or file one smaller row, and this is never counted against the asides. `off`: turning the hold off starts `delay_minutes` after asking (the chosen stake's), lasts `lasts_minutes`, then the hold comes back by itself; a stake with `job` is carried out by the AIs when the person asks off, and its `walked_away` job when the reminder ladder's `carries_stake` rung is reached (the person walked away from what waits); a newly chosen stake waits the old one's delay; each off asked within `escalate_days` multiplies the next wait by `escalate`. Every way out and its counter: src/escape-chain.json.

open_an_app._why: the owner 2026-10-08: when a Mac app road needs an app that is closed, Trillion opens it itself, in the background without taking focus (use-an-app-here.mjs openAppQuietly), so no AI files a hold asking the person to open an app. A row whose title asks to open, launch or start something (`ask`), about an app or the person's computer (`about`, read in its title and why), and which is not about Trillion itself (`except`) nor done in a Trillion screen, is refused with `refused`.
open_an_app.refused: "{title}" was not filed: opening an app on the person's computer is never theirs to do. Trillion opens the app itself, in the background without taking focus, whenever a job on their Mac needs it (use_an_app_on_this_computer or run_an_app_job); run the job and carry on. Do not file a Waiting on you row for it.

only_you_untried._why: 2026-10-09: a row said only the person could make a Cloudflare Stream token because the sign-in 'refuses automated browsers'; nobody had tried, and the coordinator made the token through the signed-in dashboard in minutes. A row that says only the person can do it (only_you_because) is kept only with `tried` saying what was attempted and what stopped it, so the claim is something an AI did, never something it assumed (src/waiting-filing.mjs invariant 8).
only_you_untried.refused: "{title}" was not filed: it says only the person can do it, but tried is empty. Try it first (their saved logins and a browser, a connected account, a tool from find_tool_for_job), then file it again with tried naming the route you took and what stopped it, word for word (the refusal, the page, the error). If a route worked, do the thing and file nothing.

no_control.refused: "{title}" was not filed: it gives the person nothing to press or do, so it could never be done. Give it do_it_in, the Trillion address where it is done, naming its target (such as /connections?show_row=<service>, the connect button for that service; a bare /connections is refused), a finish with a press, a response, or numbered steps they do by hand. If no control exists yet, build it first, or do the thing yourself.
no_control.whole_screen: "{title}" was not filed: its do_it_in {address} opens the whole screen, with every account and form on it, but the person should see only the one thing to do. A do_it_in must name its target: {path}?show_row=<the service or saved login, as titled on that screen> (or ?show_section=<section id>).
no_control.not_a_screen: "{title}" was not filed: its do_it_in {address} is not a Trillion screen, so the person would have nothing to press. Use the address of the screen where it is done, naming its target, such as /connections?show_row=<service>.
no_control.job: This was put on the person's Waiting on you list with nothing they can press or do, so it never reached them: {title}. {detail} Give it a working control, do_it_in (the Trillion address where it is done, always naming its target, such as /connections?show_row=<service> for a sign-in, which shows that service's Connect button), a finish with a press, or numbered steps, and check the control is there and works; or do it yourself. Then put the row again with put_list_rows.
no_control.said: Fixing a waiting thing that had nothing to press: {title}

rank.what: how many other waiting things wait on it, directly or through others: doing it unblocks them all

aside.job: The person set this aside instead of doing it: "{title}". Their reason: "{reason}". Weigh it: if Trillion or the person's AIs can do it, do it now and mark it done; if it is too big, cut it down to the one smallest step that takes them under a minute and put that on their Waiting on you list in its place; if it truly cannot be done now, say exactly when it can and what has to change first. Never just accept the reason.

ways.title: What did you do?
ways.placeholder: Turn on FTP sending in the camera's network menu and point it at the address shown
ways.job: The person says they did their part of "{title}" ({key}), which held their screen: "{reason}". It no longer holds them. Check it the way Trillion checks it (its done-when, the live check, the connected account, the files that should arrive); if it is done, mark the row done. If the rest is work for Trillion or the AIs (a bug, a receiver, a follow-up), do it or hand it to the AI that owns it, and say what is left. Only if the person truly must still act, put ONE new, smaller row on their Waiting on you list with a working control, saying exactly what is left and why only they can do it.

ways.label: This doesn't work here
ways.title: What happens when you try?
ways.placeholder: The Connect button keeps spinning and nothing opens
ways.job: The person could not do "{title}" ({key}), which held their screen: "{reason}". It no longer holds them. Find out why it does not work for them (its screen, its control, the connected account, the device), fix the cause, and check the fix the way they would use it. Then, if they still must act, put the row again on their Waiting on you list with a control that works and say what changed; if Trillion or the AIs can do it instead, do it and mark it done.

stakes.walked_away: Something has waited on the person for {waited} hours and they have not done it: "{first}". They chose in advance that {who} is told when they walk away from what only they can do, and {who} agreed to be.
